<pasted_content id="03dc">
Finish fixing the shell harness's `--printer-setup` run in the JusPrin repo (/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin), so it ends with `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0` and the default harness run stays at 0 failures. Then commit.

Where the work is
- Local branch `claude/printer-setup-harness-fixes` (not pushed). Its top commit `a47db8f680` is a WIP commit with the fixes so far. It sits on `claude/guide-window` (pushed; the Help › JusPrin guide window), which sits on `claude/app-guide`. Neither is on `jusprin-dev` yet.
- Make your own worktree from that branch under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/` and build it there (Release, `-j4`, `shell_integration_harness` target). Don't use another session's worktree.

What was wrong, and what the WIP commit already fixes (each one reproduced before the fix)
- Crash in `MachineObject::reset` and five Bambu connection failures in `verify_saved_bambu_connection`. Since OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 (upstream commits 159e577543c and 5028a5000e6), the device manager's nearby-printer list also holds the LAN printers of other printer agents, here the stand-in Moonraker printers (`127.0.0.1:<port>`) that earlier checks connected. The harness took `candidates.front()` as the fake Bambu printer and got a Moonraker one, so connect was refused as "other_model" and `get_my_machine(device)->reset()` dereferenced null. Fix: the new helper `lists_fake_bambu()` finds the fake by `JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_DEV_ID`, in all three fixtures that connect it.
- The nozzle-change check found no project versions: an empty project that was never saved stays in memory and keeps none (Kenneth's save rule, 74a0e9b61c). Fix: the check loads a cube first, then goes back to Home.
- The Home card check compared message text that b0a2fe3b08 replaced with the `no_connection` flag. Fix: it reads the flag.
- Closing the Add a printer chat let a waiting connection test save the printer's late answer. Fix: `PrinterConversation::close()`, called from `PrinterPanel::close()`.

What still fails: `selection_interruption_does_not_blame_credentials`
- The check connects the fake Bambu printer, calls `wxYield()` once, deselects it, and expects `connection(name)` to read state "failed" with "The selected printer changed". It reads "connecting".
- What happens during that `wxYield()`, from the app log and lldb: upstream's Device tab handles a backlog of queued `wxEVT_COMMAND_CHOICE_SELECTED` events (`MonitorPanel::on_select_printer`). There are three each for `127.0.0.1:2` and the other stand-in's port, then three more for `127.0.0.1:2`; all are refused as "not in the current agent's machine list". Then one for `FAKE001`, which takes upstream's "same LAN machine: disconnect and reconnect" path. The fake answers the disconnect with ConnectStatusLost, and upstream's local-connect handler (GUI_App.cpp, about line 2470) clears the selection. The backend then sees a Lost answer newer than the connect, reports it before looking at the selection (OrcaPrinterBackend::connection, about line 678), and holds "connecting" while its port look runs.
- Who queues them: upstream `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent()` → `GUI_App::select_machine()` → `MonitorPanel::select_machine()`, which only queues the event. It runs each time a printer preset loads during the earlier `verify_named_printers` checks (for example from `Printers::rename_named_printer` → `Tab::load_config`).
- Open question to settle first: why aren't those queued events handled when they are queued? The harness waits with a one-shot wxTimer, so the event loop should run between checks. Find out whether a real person can hit the same thing (selections piling up behind a hidden Device tab, then clearing a Bambu connection), or whether only the harness's way of driving the app causes it. That decides whether the fix belongs in the harness or in the app. If the fix touches an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` first.

How to run, and the traps already hit
- `cd build/arm64; HOME=<your scratch>/hhome ./tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup > <log> 2>&1`. A run takes 5–25 minutes, longer when the machine is loaded, so run it in the background.
- Run one harness at a time, and never delete the HOME folder of a run that is still going. Two runs at once, sharing one HOME, gave extra timing failures (the host-timeout checks and `home_bambu_error_pause_needs_attention`) that are not real. Check `pgrep -fl JusPrinShellHarness` before every start.
- Check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building. Load from other sessions reached 24 on 12 cores and makes the host-timeout checks flaky.
- The app log is in the run's data dir (`HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: …` at the end of the output), under `log/`. Delete only the data dirs your own runs print.
- In this Release build lldb can't read arguments by name. For `set_selected_machine(std::string)` use `memory read -f s -c 1 '$x1+1'` (a short string's text starts one byte in) and `bt`.
- After restoring a file from a copy, `touch` it, or ninja won't recompile it.

Done when
- `--printer-setup` passes with 0 failures, twice in a row, each run on its own.
- The default harness run (no flag) passes with 0 failures.
- The fix for the last check is reproduced failing before and passing after.
- The include check passes on the changed lines: `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh`.
- The WIP commit is replaced by a finished commit (or commits) on `claude/printer-setup-harness-fixes`, with a message that says what was wrong, how it was fixed, and what was tested.
- Don't push or open a PR unless Kenneth asks. Report to Kenneth in his style: under 500 words, outcomes not the journey, and any decision asked in full starting with "Decision needed".

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata:

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.

---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

Shell harness --printer-setup passes again after the OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 merge

`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup` had seven failing checks and a
crash in MachineObject::reset. All were reproduced before fixing. Six
were the harness reading app state that the 2.5.0 merge and later fork
commits changed. One was a real app bug: a late answer from a printer
was saved into a chat that had been closed.

- The Bambu connection fixtures now pick the fake printer by its id
  (new helper lists_fake_bambu). Since OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 (upstream
  159e577543c, 5028a5000e6) the device manager's nearby-printer list
  also holds other printer agents' LAN printers. Here those were the
  stand-in Moonraker printers (127.0.0.1:<port>) that earlier checks
  connected. Taking the first entry picked one of them, so the connect
  was refused as another model, and
  get_my_machine(...)->reset() dereferenced a null machine.
- The nozzle-change check loads a cube first. A project that was never
  saved stays in memory and keeps no versions (74a0e9b61c), so the
  check found none.
- The Home card check reads the no_connection flag, which replaced the
  message text it compared (b0a2fe3b08).
- App fix: closing the Add a printer chat now ends a connection test
  that is still waiting (PrinterConversation::close, called from
  PrinterPanel::close), so the printer's late answer is not saved into
  a chat that no longer exists.
- selection_interruption_does_not_blame_credentials waits for the event
  loop to settle before connecting. The fake printer is already listed
  from earlier checks, so the check's wait used to end at once, and
  saving the printer, selecting its preset and connecting all ran in
  one event turn. The Device tab selections that the preset loads
  queued (GUI_App::select_machine -> MonitorPanel::select_machine) then
  ran after the connect. They re-selected the fake printer mid-connect
  and took upstream's "same LAN machine: disconnect and reconnect"
  path. The fake answered Lost, upstream cleared the selection, and the
  connection read "connecting" instead of "The selected printer
  changed". A person cannot hit this: a connect comes from its own
  tool call, in a later event turn than the preset load. With the real
  Bambu agent, GUI_App::select_machine reconnects directly and queues
  nothing, and upstream's in-flight guard (#17086) keeps a connect
  that is still running. Only the fake, which runs under its own agent
  id, goes through the Device tab queue.
- printer_panel_greeting_continues_with_the_composer waits up to 30 s
  for the page to show the composer, as the panel's other page checks
  do. The page learns of the new AI in a message and renders on its own
  schedule. Under load (load average 20-30 on 12 cores) a single read
  saw the old offer screen.

  changed lines.
